newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision Garden deal pays off -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision Garden deal pays off -- analysts.

text.p: By inking its sports TV deal with Fox Liberty Networks, Cablevision Systems Corp has succeeded in making its purchase of the Madison Square Garden sports properties pay off, analysts said on Monday.
"The valuation (of the Fox deal) was attractive," said Spencer Grimes at Smith Barney. "It certainly validates, confirms the value of the MSG properties."

Cablevision will receive $850 million from Fox/Liberty for a 40 percent stake in the sports interests of its Rainbow Media Holdings Inc unit, including MSG and the various regional SportsChannel networks.

The deal helps Cablevision further cut its debt. "It reinforces their commitment to shareholders," said David Doft, an analyst at Furman Selz. "It's a plus for the balance sheet." Cablevision shares added 1/4 to 53-3/8.
Cablevision vice chairman Marc Lustgarten told reporters the company will use the proceeds to reduce the $1.25 billion in debt it incurred when Rainbow bought MSG.

In April, Cablevision signed a definitive deal to buy out ITT Corp's 50 percent partnership in MSG, which includes basketball and hockey teams and the MSG televison network. The companies teamed up in 1995 to buy the Garden for $1 billion.

The announcement of the Fox deal was the second in a month by Cablevision. On June 9, it said it was buying Tele-Communication Inc's New York cable operations with 820,000 subscribers in exchange for 33 percent of Cablevision's outstanding stock.

Analysts said they expected Cablevision to make other announcements that would raise more cash to cut debt -- through the sales of cable TV systems with more than 400,000 subscribers. "They still have a couple of more announcements (to make)" Grimes said.

Grimes said the future deals would cheer Wall Street. "Investors like private market value asset sales," he said, adding that the deals would likely fetch higher prices than if the properties were sold as separate public entities.

Fox's venture with Rainbow will include national, regional and local sports programming, reaching 55 million homes under the name Fox Sports Net. It will appear on nine Fox/Liberty regional cable TV networks, eight Rainbow regional sports channels, and the Fox Sports regional sports systems.
Analysts said it would be difficult to estimate how much advertising revenue would be derived under the Fox Sports banner. But they saw it as a plus.

"It's always been terribly inconvenient for advertisers to buy a regional (sports program) because no one was clear as to what TV markets would be able to watch it, and how wide the distribution was," Grimes said. "This makes it easier for ad buyers. They can buy all 55 million homes or a local team."

Lustgarten shied away from projecting how much in revenues the new venture would generate for Cablevision, which owns 75 percent of Rainbow. "Only time will tell," he said. But he said the new venture "should create a great deal more cash flow."
Fox/Liberty is a joint venture of News Corp's Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp, a unit of Tele-Communications.
